source_findings: uniprof is a TypeScript/Node wrapper that selects platform/runtime profilers and normalizes their outputs into a common profile/analysis flow.

Supported underlying profilers include py-spy, 0x, rbspy, Excimer, async-profiler, dotnet-trace, perf, and macOS Instruments; these remain separate third-party components with their own licenses and runtime requirements.
The default operational model prefers Docker containers for setup isolation/reproducibility; host mode is supported when profiler dependencies are already present.
The codebase guide documents a PlatformPlugin contract plus ProfileContext/raw-artifact/post-processing lifecycle, which is the most transferable structural idea for F2 profiling.
Sampling defaults are approximately 999 Hz on several supported profilers, so profiler overhead and sampling-frequency bias must itself be measured rather than assumed negligible.
Some profiler paths can require elevated privileges; native Linux profiling depends on perf and host/kernel policy.
The npm package imports MCP SDK and CLI/UI dependencies that are not required merely to establish an F2 profiling evidence contract.
hypothesis: A common normalized profile artifact and per-runtime adapter contract can make F2 CPU hotspot evidence reproducible across modules without coupling the architecture to one profiler.
counterhypothesis: Importing uniprof as the default runtime path would add Node/Docker/container/privilege/dependency overhead, may perturb the workload being measured, and duplicates functionality that can be achieved more cheaply by invoking the smallest runtime-native profiler and normalizing only the evidence schema.

distill: explicit sampling-rate/profiler identity in every receipt
do_not_promote_yet: Docker as default F2 profiling authority
cross-language tool adoption before equivalent-overhead measurement
acceptance_falsifiers_for_future_e2_e3: normalized schema loses profiler-specific timing semantics
wrapper/container overhead materially changes hotspot ranking
direct py-spy/perf/other native invocation is simpler and equally reproducible
privilege requirements make the route non-portable across the intended F2 environment
